lesson_title: Repo Rate vs the Budget: Who Fights Inflation?
hook_text: One number set in Pretoria changes your family's home loan. Here's the chain.
clip_script: Link one: the repo rate rises, so borrowing from the SARB costs the commercial banks more. Link two: the banks pass that cost on by raising their prime lending rate — the rate they charge their own customers. Repo up, prime up, almost immediately. Link three: loans throughout the economy become more expensive. Home loan instalments rise. Car finance costs more. Link four: households and firms cut back. Link five: total spending in the economy slows. With less money chasing goods and services, the upward pressure on prices eases, and inflation drifts back toward the target band.
visual_style: Falling-dominoes animation: each link a domino labelled repo, prime, loans, spending, prices, toppling in sequence.
pacing: Rapid-fire links with a breath before the final domino settles.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master both policy toolboxes.
